description.value: This baseline cross-sectional study examined Negative Affectivity-related resting-state ALFF and functional connectivity patterns in depressed and never-depressed older adults.

spans.text: Therefore, we sought to examine relationships between neuroticism and resting state functional activity and connectivity (rsFC) among older adults with and without major depression who were enrolled in the Neurobiology of Late-life Depression study (NBOLD).

value: We hypothesized that presence of high Negativity Affectivity (NA), a key feature of neuroticism, would be associated with different prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity and connectivity patterns in depressed and never-depressed older adults.
we hypothesized that higher NA in never-depressed older adults would show different dmPFC and vmPFC activity and connectivity patterns from depressed adults.
